exercise1.prompt: Year, month and weekday are columns you can group by.

hiddenCases.name: a single month gives a single entry
the same month in different years still shares a bucket

exercise1.hint: Group by df["day"].dt.month and sum n. The second hidden case is a warning about that: month alone ignores the year, which is sometimes what you want and sometimes a bug.

questions.prompt: Grouping by month alone across two years does what?
choices: Puts both Marches in the same bucket
questions.explain: The month number carries no year. Grouping by year and month together is what you want for a timeline.

choices: A number for the day of the week
questions.explain: Monday is 0. day_name() gives the text when you want it readable.

questions.prompt: Why is a date part just an ordinary column?
choices: Because it is values, so everything that works on a column works on it
questions.explain: Once the part is a value you can group, filter, sort and plot with it exactly as with anything else.
